# Slider

> A single-thumb slider built on the native range input.

`<slab-slider>` · Form · built on `<input type=range>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/slider/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/slider.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-slider
  label="Volume"
  name="volume"
  min="0"
  max="100"
  value="50"
></slab-slider>
```

Screenreaders read the value as a bare number. When it means more than that, set `formatValue` to a function of the value, such as `` (value) => `$${value}` ``, and they'll read what it returns instead.

Its value is always in range, so it's never invalid on its own. For a rule of your own, such as a minimum, call `setCustomValidity()` with a message. It shows in `::part(validity-message)`, and the host matches `:state(error)`, once validity is reported, as on [Text Field](text-field.md): when focus leaves, when its form is submitted, or on `reportValidity()`.

## Keyboard

| Key                   | What it does                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Left, Down, Right, Up | Steps the value down or up, as on a range input. |
| Page Up, Page Down    | Steps it by more, where the browser does.        |
| Home, End             | Moves to the minimum or maximum.                 |

## Elements

### `<slab-slider>`

Import `slab-elements/slider.js` to register it.

A single-thumb slider with no visual styles, around a native range input, so it is dragged, stepped with the keyboard, and read the way one is.

The label and the input are both in the shadow root, so a plain `for` reference names it without crossing out of one. The host delegates focus, so clicking anywhere on it, or a `<label for>` pointing at it, focuses the input.

The value is the native input's. `min`, `max` and `step` are passed through to it, and `value` is read back from it, so a value outside the range or off a step is clamped and snapped the way a range input does it. With no value, it sits halfway between `min` and `max`, as a range input does.

Screenreaders read the value as a number. Set `formatValue` to a function of it that says what it means, such as "$40" or "3 of 5 GB", which becomes the input's `aria-valuetext`.

Its value is always in range, so it's never invalid on its own. For a rule of your own, such as a minimum, call `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`. The validity message shows in its description, as on Text Field, once validity is reported: when focus leaves it, its form is submitted, or `reportValidity()` is called.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(disabled)` and `:state(error)`. Where the label sits relative to the input is layout, so it's left to the styles around it.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type              | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`          |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                      |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`         | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                                                                      |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean`         | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                   |
| `max`              | `number`          |         | 100 when unset, as on a range input.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `min`              | `number`          |         | 0 when unset, as on a range input.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `name`             | `string`          | `''`    | The name its value is submitted under, as a native control's `name`.                                                                                                                               |
| `step`             | `number \| 'any'` |         | A number, or "any" to allow any value. Left unset, the input's own default of 1 applies.                                                                                                           |
| `value`            | `string`          | `''`    | Like a native input, the attribute is the default value and the property is the current one. The property is always the value the input settled on, so it's never outside the range or off a step. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                                     | Description                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formatValue`                   | `(value: number) => string \| undefined` | What screenreaders read for the value, such as "$40" rather than "40". The value itself when unset.                                   |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null`                | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                    |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                                 | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`. Empty while it's valid. |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`                          | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                           |
| `valueAsNumber`                 | `number`                                 | `value` as a number, as on a native range input.                                                                                      |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                                | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                     |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                   |
| `click(): void`                                                   | Clicks it, as a native element's `click()` does.                                                                              |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                               |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.   |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                     |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                    |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`. |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.               |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.             |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown. |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description` | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | Text about the slider, and its validity message when it has one |
| `input`            | The input                                                       |
| `label`            | The label                                                       |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid       |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(error)`    | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
